description: A small diff adds an update route whose ownership check uses findUnique on id only (userId is read but never used to scope the lookup) — a cross-tenant update leak. The reviewer must surface this as a Critical/High security finding with a file:line reference, per its Security Audit dimension (authorization correctness).

dispatch_context.task: Review this recently changed file before commit. The diff adds a PUT /:id route to the notes API.
dispatch_context.diff:
--- a/fixtures/src/notes-routes.ts
+++ b/fixtures/src/notes-routes.ts
@@ -5,6 +5,17 @@ const app = new Hono()
 
+app.put('/:id', async (c) => {
+  const id = c.req.param('id')
+  const userId = c.get('userId')
+  const body = await c.req.json()
+  const note = await prisma.note.findUnique({ where: { id } })
+  if (!note) return apiError(c, 'Not found', 404)
+  const updated = await prisma.note.update({ where: { id }, data: { title: body.title } })
+  return apiSuccess(c, updated)
+})
+
 export default app

rubric_hints.trigger_reliability: Agent treats the dispatch as a code review (not a Q&A), reads the provided diff/file, and systematically applies its five concern areas — the Security Audit dimension (authentication and authorization correctness) is the one that must fire here
rubric_hints.output_structure: Return matches the documented Code Review Report: Scope with files reviewed + review type, Overall Assessment, Findings grouped by severity with file:line references and a fix suggestion, Metrics with issue counts — not a freeform paragraph
rubric_hints.non_negotiable_adherence: Flat-worker default honored: dispatched normally (no 'mode: nested-verify' in the prompt), so the agent must NOT spawn verifier subagents via Agent(); it reviews and returns its findings flat
rubric_hints.side_effect_correctness: PRIMARY BUG CHECK: the missing ownership scoping is found — the lookup uses findUnique on id alone while userId is read and never used, so any authenticated user can update another tenant's note; the finding must be Critical or High, point at fixtures/src/notes-routes.ts with the offending line, and recommend an ownership-scoped lookup (e.g. findFirst with both id and userId). No fixture file is modified — the agent reviews, it does not edit
rubric_hints.error_propagation: The defect is reported as a prioritized finding with severity and actionable fix, not softened into a Low/style note, not omitted because the code 'runs fine' — a review that returns zero Critical/High findings here is the failure mode under test
